Annotation.description:
A root comment anchored to a place in a document. Returned when you create or
patch one and as the items of the comment lists. Replies are shallow and nested
under the root comment.

document_id.description:
The document the comment is anchored to. Stable — a comment is pinned to the
document id, not its path, so renaming or moving the document never orphans the
comment. A comment can't move between documents.

anchor.description:
The selection the comment is pinned to — an **opaque, client-owned** object the
server stores and returns exactly as received. The server never parses,
validates, or re-anchors it (`additionalProperties: true` is intentional).
When document text changes, a client may reattach the comment and replace this
whole object with `PATCH .../annotations/{annoId}`.

body.description: The comment text, a plain string (no rich text; image attachments ride the separate `attachments` field).

attachments.description:
Image attachments on the comment: absolute `https://` URLs, in the order
they were attached, at most 8. Present only when the comment carries at
least one attachment; omitted otherwise (older comments serve
byte-identical responses). The server stores the URLs verbatim and never
fetches, proxies, or resizes them. Clients normally point them at the
hash-pinned asset `url` the asset upload route returned, so the image
keeps rendering for every later reader.

author.description:
A display label for who wrote the comment — **never** used to decide who can
delete it. For a logged-in or API-key caller it is server-derived from the
authenticated identity. For an anonymous commenter on a `link_edit` document it's an
optional self-supplied name, or `null` if none was given (and is therefore
unverified — render it as untrusted text, like the body).

author_name.description:
The comment author's human display name, stamped at write time from the
authenticated identity's profile (never the email). Omitted or `null` when no
name is known: anonymous comments (their optional self-supplied name is in
`author`), identities whose login provider carries no profile name, and
comments written before names were recorded. Display only — when absent,
render your existing `author` convention; never treat it as an identifier.

agent.description:
Formal agent attribution for a row written by an **agent credential** — an API
key, or an MCP OAuth token on deployments that enable the MCP OAuth arm. When
this object is present, the row's `author`
(or actor/requester id field) is formally the **on-behalf-of human**: the
delegating user's id, and the agent named here is the actual author. Derived
entirely from stored credential facts at write time — never client-supplied.
Omitted (never null-filled) on rows a human wrote directly and on rows written
before agent attribution was recorded.

id.description:
The agent's stable principal id — the API key id (`key_…`) for `api_key`
writes; the token id (JWT `jti`), else the OAuth client id, else the
approving user's id for `mcp_token` writes. A formal id-backed linkage,
not a display string.

kind.description:
The stored credential kind behind the write. Derive any "agent" marker
from THIS fact (plus `id`), never from `name` — agent names are
registrant-chosen and can look human.

name.description:
The agent's own display name — the API key's user-typed name — stamped
at write time, never an email. `null` when the credential carried no
safe display name (always `null` for `mcp_token` writes today); the
`id` linkage still holds. Untrusted display text.

review_submission_id.description:
The approval submission this comment belongs to — the author's
feedback batch on the round that was open when the comment was
written — or `null`: no round was open, the author was anonymous,
or the comment predates the feature. Server-assigned at write
time, never accepted on create or PATCH, and never re-decided.
`null` again if the submission's round is later pruned. Clients
use it to group the comment index under the approval panel.

state.description:
The root comment's thread state. `resolved` hides or dims the thread in clients
and blocks new replies; it does not prevent cleanup edits/deletes.

updated_at.description: When the root comment body, state, or anchor last changed.

replies.description: Shallow replies under this root comment, oldest first.

items.description: A shallow reply under a root comment.

annotation_id.description: The root comment this reply belongs to.

body.description: The reply text — a plain string, no rich text or attachments.

author.description:

server-derived attribution; anonymous link_edit-doc callers may pass a display name.

author_name.description:

authenticated identity's profile (never the email). Omitted or `null` when no
name is known — render your existing `author` convention instead.

review_submission_id.description:
The REPLIER's approval submission — a reply joins the replier's
own feedback batch, never the root author's — or `null`; same
rules as the root comment's field. Server-assigned, never
accepted from the caller.

updated_at.description: When the reply body last changed.

doc_path.description:
The document's current path — **present on the workspace-wide list**
(`GET /v1/workspaces/{wsId}/annotations`) **and the org-wide list**
(`GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/annotations`), as a display label so you can group
comments by document. It's recomputed on every read and is **not stable** (a
rename changes it): never key, cache, or address by it — use `document_id`.
Omitted on the per-document list and the create response.

workspace_id.description:
The workspace the comment lives in — **present only on the org-wide list**
(`GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/annotations`), where comments span many workspaces, so
each one can be traced to its workspace. Omitted everywhere else (the
workspace is already fixed by the path).

CreateAnnotationRequest.description: The body for adding a comment to a document. The whole JSON request is capped at 32 KiB.

anchor.description:
The selection to pin the comment to — an opaque, client-owned object stored and
returned verbatim (the server never looks inside it), with one exception:
`point`. Required. Serialized JSON form must be at most 16 KiB of UTF-8.

If the anchor carries a top-level `point` key, it must be the normalized
pinpoint `{x, y}`: each coordinate a finite number from 0 to 1 inclusive,
measured inside the anchored target's rectangle. An out-of-range,
non-finite, or non-numeric
coordinate is rejected with the standard `validation_error` shape naming
the offending field (for example `anchor.point.x`). Keys beside `x`/`y`
inside `point`, and anchors without a `point` key, stay fully opaque.

point.description: Optional normalized pinpoint inside the anchored target's rectangle, `0..1` per axis.

body.description: The comment text, a plain string, at most 8 KiB of UTF-8.

attachments.description:
Optional image attachments: at most 8 absolute `https://` URLs, each at
most 2048 characters. An entry that does not parse as an `https` URL
(plain `http`, `javascript:`, `data:`, a bare filename) is rejected with
the standard `validation_error` shape. Stored verbatim and returned on
every read of the comment. Upload the image first (asset upload route)
and put its returned hash-pinned `url` here.

author.description:
Optional display name, honored only for an anonymous commenter on a `link_edit`
document. For a logged-in or API-key caller the server uses the authenticated
identity and ignores this field (so attribution can't be spoofed). At most 120
characters.

PatchAnnotationRequest.description:
A partial update to a root comment. Include any combination of `body`, `state`,
and `anchor`. `anchor` is full replacement, not merge-patch. The whole JSON
request is capped at 32 KiB.

anchor.description:
Replacement opaque anchor object. Serialized JSON form must be at most 16 KiB
of UTF-8. The create-time `point` rule applies here too: a top-level `point`
key, if present, must carry finite normalized `x`/`y` coordinates in `0..1`
(see `CreateAnnotationRequest.anchor`).

point.description: Optional normalized pinpoint inside the anchored target's rectangle, `0..1` per axis.

body.description: Replacement comment text, at most 8 KiB of UTF-8.
body.example: This paragraph now has a citation.

state.description: Open or resolve the root comment thread.

Error.description: The standard error shape. Errors are always JSON.

code.description: The set of error codes the API can return.

details.description:
Optional extra information about the error. The object is free-form
(`additionalProperties: true`), with two schema-**typed** exceptions you
can rely on as real fields: `version_conflict` carries
`details.current_version` (see `VersionConflictError`), the one an agent
must branch on to retry, and `validation_error` carries `details.fields`,
a map of field name → what's wrong (see `ValidationErrorBody`). The rest
are documented, best-effort hints on the same free-form object — a
`path_conflict` carries `details.doc_path`.
